svg.aria-label: Schematic: Arduino Uno interface for the E36 cluster
svg.text: E36 cluster interface: Arduino Uno -> VDO 62.11-8 360 482
All cluster outputs pull the cluster pin to ground (low-side switch). The Uno is powered by USB only, 12 V never goes to the Uno (no VIN, no 5V).
Net labels with the same name are connected. Cluster pins use the numbers printed on the cluster (white = J2, blue = J3, black = J4).
KL15 -> white 23 and blue 4 (blue 5 left open)
GND -> white 24, blue 3, blue 17, black 3 and Uno GND
Not connected on purpose: KL R (white 15, blue 16), blue 5 and 6 (charge lamp),
2 Signal outputs: IRLZ34N low-side switch (RPM and speed proven on the real cluster)
Optional (not fitted): C3/C4 1 uF from the coolant and fuel output to GND, only if the needle jitters.
3 Lamp outputs: two ULN2803A (14 of 16 channels used)
Each lamp line: Uno pin -> ULN input (internal 2.7 kOhm and pull-down, no extra parts),
ULN output -> 470 Ohm -> cluster pin. The ULN pulls the pin to about 1 V (Darlington).
The 470 Ohm makes the lamps glow dim. After the polarity test, bridge the resistor (wire) per lamp.
1. Order of the build: power section first (no cluster plugged in), check LED1/LED2, then the signal outputs one by one.
2. Check the supply polarity with the board: with reversed supply D1 blocks, LED1 stays dark and nothing is damaged.
3. All grounds are one net: J1 GND, Uno GND, all MOSFET sources, ULN pin 9, cluster ground pins.
4. Cluster pins are numbered as printed on the cluster (white 26/1/13 and 14/1, black 12/6 and 7/1). Check twice.
5. Never connect the cluster outputs blue 2, 9, 10, 24 (they drive other equipment, not inputs).
6. Gate pull-downs 10 kOhm go to GND (as built). The optional pull-up variant to 5 V is described in docs/e36-uno.md.
7. Lamp polarity (pin to ground = lamp on) and the PWM coolant/fuel circuit are assumptions: verify with the multimeter.
8. The Uno stays USB-powered. D13 drives the onboard LED too, the right turn signal may blink once at Uno reset. Harmless.
9. Uno pins used: D2-D13 and A0-A5. D0/D1 stay free for USB.
X1 Arduino Uno (plugs under the shield)
Uno pins: D2-D13, A0-A5 (as digital outputs), GND -> board ground
5V: not used (only for the optional pull-up variant)
Cluster side: J2 white 2x13, J3 blue 2x13, J4 black 2x6, numbered 1:1 as on the cluster.
J2/J3/J4 connect to the mating connectors (pigtails) of the cluster, see README.
